text: The first image is a style and character reference: match its look, the same woman (treasure hunter in her 30s, short dark hair, sun-worn linen shirt, leather satchel), the same volcanic shore and rowboat. Cinematic live-action footage, anamorphic lens, subtle 35mm film grain, moody teal-and-amber grade, shallow depth of field. One continuous handheld tracking shot: she steps out of the wooden rowboat onto wet black sand, takes three steps up the beach, then stops and glances back over her shoulder toward the camera, an antique brass compass in her hand. Waves break behind her, sea spray, wind in her hair. No cuts. No dialogue. No music; only wind, surf and footsteps.

Cinematic live-action macro footage, 35mm film grain, golden-hour rim light, shallow depth of field. Extreme close-up of an antique brass MAGNETIC COMPASS held open in a weathered hand. The dial is white enamel with a printed compass rose and the cardinal letters N, E, S, W and a degree ring. There is exactly ONE slender steel needle on a central pivot, blued steel on its north half. NO clock numerals, NO clock hands, NO Roman numerals, NO minute track. The needle swings left and right, slows, and settles pointing firmly toward the letter W, not north. Locked-off camera, slow push-in. No dialogue. No music; only wind and a faint metallic tick.
